Get started.

Review the source. Understand the trade-offs. Follow the steps at your own pace.

Local Python tool
Read this before you begin.

This script sends fabricated game activity using your Discord account credentials. Discord forbids automated user accounts and may terminate accounts that use them. It is unofficial and not supported by Discord. Read Discord’s policy ↗

Python 3.10+ A local terminal Sensitive credentials required Nothing runs on this page

Start with the right environment.

This is a command-line Python program, not code for Discord’s browser console. It attempts to inflate Game Time and Game Variety; it does not implement Streaming or Account Age progression.

  • Install Python 3.10 or newer. No pip packages are required.
  • Use a writable folder and an internet connection. The game catalog is downloaded automatically if needed.
  • The optional fingerprint generator requires Windows and PowerShell. Other platforms cannot use that feature.
Get Python from python.org

Keep the complete file together.

Review the source in the editor, then copy it into a plain-text file named spoofer.py. Save it as UTF-8. You can also download the same original file.

The copy action uses the whole file, including content outside the collapsed preview. It does not run the code.

Download .py

After copying, continue to step 3 to open it locally.

Open your terminal in that folder.

In Terminal, Command Prompt, or PowerShell, open the folder containing spoofer.py. The README’s launch command is:

python spoofer.py

Your python command must point to Python 3.10+. If it is missing or points to an older version, resolve your Python installation first.

Launching the file starts local prompts and may make network requests. The website never launches it for you.

Know what the local prompts ask for.

On first run, the program requires your account token and a cookie header containing cf_clearance. The README assumes you already have these; it references a Discord client request’s Cookie header.

These are sensitive credentials. Do not paste them into this website, a support message, or a browser console. If you do not understand or accept that access, stop here.

Plaintext storage, real requests.

The script writes credentials to science_state.json beside itself and sends authenticated requests to Discord. Never share or upload that file. Its optional third-party properties request does not include credentials in the inspected code.

Follow the actual on-screen menu.

1
Claim gamesChoose a game count and hours per game. Blank inputs default to all loaded games and 1 hour. Use positive, finite numbers.
2
Refresh authRefresh the analytics token and optionally update the cookie.
3
Set fingerprintOptional Windows-only generation using a game executable or process ID. It reads executable metadata and a device identifier to create an account-bound fingerprint.
4
ExitLeave the menu. A blank menu selection also exits.

The supplied README’s separate “games played” option is outdated. Some in-script error hints also give the old menu number: auth refresh is option 2.

Separate sent events from earned badges.

A 204 response means a request was accepted. “Claimed” totals in the terminal are local counters, not confirmation that Discord awarded progress.

The README reports a 1–2 day delay, but neither that timing nor current effectiveness has been verified here. There is no guaranteed result. Check Discord’s own Badge Directory for actual account progress.

The optional fingerprint’s effect is also uncertain in the README. Do not treat repeated submissions as proof of success.

Find your Badge Directory
Step 1 of 6
Before you troubleshoot

Auth rejected? The actual refresh action is menu option 2, even if an old error hint says 3.

Game list unavailable? Check the connection and writable folders. The program downloads Discord’s catalog and attempts to cache it at ../data/games.json, relative to the script’s folder.

Fingerprint not set? It is optional in the implementation. Generation is Windows-only and its impact on badge credit is not guaranteed.

Debug output? The provided file has DEBUG = False. Enabling debug can print authentication headers. Never share logs containing credentials.

Checked October 27, 2026. Official mechanics: Discord’s badge guide, badge management guide, and personalization settings.

Ten-tier names, artwork mappings, and thresholds are community documented by Discord Badge Archive, cross-checked with Infinity Hub’s tier list. Discord’s official guide does not enumerate these tier tables. Treat them as a reference, not guaranteed unlock requirements. The top tier is shown as a minimum threshold, with “+”.

Discord badge artwork is mirrored from dev-hoehle/discord-badges; all Discord marks belong to Discord. The featured sunset banner and avatar are AI-created adaptations of a community member’s supplied profile reference. Featured badges are interactive illustrations, not a live account readout. The playground avatar and Badgecraft identity are original, unofficial illustrations. Badgecraft itself collects no analytics or credentials and makes no Discord API requests. The separate Python program makes authenticated requests when a visitor runs it locally, as explained in the script guide.
